blocks.content: The rock cycle is the continuous process through which rocks transform from one type to another over geological time.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The rock cycle is a continuous geological process through which Earth's materials transform between igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic forms over millions of years.
Igneous rocks are formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava and serve as primary rocks from which all other rocks originate.
Sedimentary rocks form through weathering, erosion, deposition, compaction, and cementation (lithification) of rock debris.
Metamorphic rocks result from the alteration of existing rocks under intense heat, pressure, and chemical tectonic action without actual melting.
Subduction carries surface rocks into the Earth's interior, melting them into magma and restarting the continuous rock cycle.

blocks.content: Rocks do not remain in their original form for long but undergo a continuous transformation, driving the endless cycle of the Earth's crust.
• Magma cools to form igneous rocks.

rows: Cooling and solidification of magma or lava
Crystalline structure, non-foliated, contains no fossils
Deposition, compaction, and lithification of debris
Stratified layers, soft texture, frequently contains fossils
Transformation of existing rocks under high heat and pressure
Foliated or banded structure, hard and dense, no fossils

blocks.content: • Sediments compact to form sedimentary rocks.
• Heat and pressure convert rocks into metamorphic rocks.

items: Igneous rocks are called Primary Rocks because all other rock types are directly or indirectly formed from them.
Fossils are found almost exclusively in Sedimentary Rocks, as the high heat and pressure in igneous and metamorphic formations destroy organic traces.
Lithification refers specifically to the process of converting loose sediments into consolidated sedimentary rocks through compaction and cementation.

blocks.content: • Metamorphic rocks may melt again to form magma.
The rock cycle demonstrates that no rock type is permanent.
